recovery_sequence: Prefer recovered local board and native files. Otherwise start from the exact published working commit, preserve it and export geometry with native_board.py.

First proposal used route_control_R134.py with grid0.1mm and A*visit cap500000, unchanged0.2mm traces, RF/USB-reference and B thermal keepout masks. It yielded seven successful connections: CHG_EN1_CMD,CHG_EN2_CMD,CHG_CE_CMD,two mode-support links and two GND links. Apply only the successful routes.
Remove the12 exact obsolete EN1 VBUS-supply copper items declared below. This disconnects actual U3 IN until its supply is reconnected; it must not be left open.
Remove the exact REG_PG B segment and CHG_STAT2 F segment below to open routing corridors. Both nets must be rerouted and verified.

Route CHG_EN1,CHG_EN2,CHG_CE_N,VBUS_USB,REG_PG and CHG_STAT2 with local bounds x39..62,y75..104mm, continuous copper checks and at least0.2mm digital/0.3mm VBUS tracks. The experimental0.15mm widths are rejected.
Apply only legal continuous routes with native_board.py. Tent every new ordinary through via both sides; preserve the original five U3 thermal-via filled/capped requests.

Run full native DRC with schematic parity, all track errors and zone refill, save board, export geometry. Prune obsolete leaves with connectivity checks. Only16 unchanged button-hole findings are the intended unresolved native baseline.
Run complete native ERC and full independent audits. Freeze the actual new source SHA and checkpoint only after successful comparison. Publish and obtain a fresh R134 server CI artifact.
